newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia protesters dodge police in Burma protest.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia protesters dodge police in Burma protest.

text.p: Cambodia's opposition Khmer Nation Party (KNP) on Wednesday dodged government efforts to prevent a protest against visiting Burmese leader General Than Shwe and his military junta.

Two or three shots were fired in the air as a group of about 100 protesters neared the U.S. Embassy, but witnesses said nobody appeared to have been injured. It was also not clear who fired the shots.
KNP leader Sam Rainsy went into the embassy to deliver a message to Ambassador Kenneth Quin explaining the purpose of his march and asking for support, the witnesses added.
The authorities had sealed off the KNP headquarters with scores of police, barricades and a waste truck shortly before Than Shwe's scheduled arrival on an official four-day visit.

But witnesses said about 100 people, led by Sam Rainsy, eluded police and marched through other parts of Phnom Penh with banners denouncing the Burmese government and backing democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

The protesters had earlier this week written to the interior ministry saying they planned to march past parliament and the Independence Monument. Heavy police deployments on Wednesday blocked the planned march route.
Municipal authorities, citing security, said on Tuesday they would not allow the protest march. Sam Rainsy, who met Suu Kyi in Rangoon in August, had later said they would go ahead anyhow.
The Rangoon government recently barred Suu Kyi, a Nobel Peace laureate, from giving regular weekend speeches at her home and blocked a congress planned for her National League for Democracy party.
It also arrested hundreds of party activists and later released them in stages.

Than Shwe is scheduled to meet King Norodom Sihanouk, co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen and other officials during his first visit to Cambodia since diplomatic ties were restored in 1994, officials said.
Children waving Burmese and Cambodian flags lined the main boulevard of the capital ahead of his arrival.
